title: Polynomial multipliers of differentiation-hypercyclic functions
actual: Read all four native PDF pages visually and as searchable text, and all controlling TeX against the exact support ZIP.
proof: A dense meagre family in H(C) consists of differentiation-hypercyclic entire functions f such that for every fixed nonconstant complex polynomial p the sequence |(pf)^(n)(0)| tends to infinity. The universal preserving multipliers are exactly the nonzero constants. The onset depends on p.

On a closed nonempty annular jet subspace, any relatively open disk neighborhood can retain its finite prefix and program a distant finite target block, moving small or zero coefficients at most the decreasing inner bound. Factorial tails yield uniform convergence and quantitative control of D^N. Baire inside each complete X_M, then polynomial approximation as M grows, yields ambient density; each X_M is nowhere dense. There is no invariance or uncountable category intersection requirement.

Leibniz gives falling-factorial multipliers with leading order ≥const n^{d−1/2} and all earlier terms O(n^{d−1} log n). Reverse triangle handles arbitrary complex phases. Evaluation at zero gives a non-dense scalar orbit after avoiding the finite prefix. The universal failure result and residual common good family coexist.

Nikula gives near-sure frequent hypercyclicity for IID full-support Gaussian jets. The exponent 3/4 ensures summable low hits; the logarithmic upper bound has summable violations. Radial clipping yields a null-orbit correction and a full-support law on X_M with the possible degenerate unit circle at n=0. The earlier Gaussian-eigenfield route follows from the cited Bayart–Matheron proposition with the exponential eigenfield.
